title: Finite refinement of a surjective etale morphism
statement:
Let $u:U\to T$ be a surjective etale morphism
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and assume that $T$ is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. There exist a finite set $J$, a finite, finitely presented,
surjective morphism

$$
 r:T'\longrightarrow T,
$$

a finite open covering $T'=\bigcup_{a\in J}W_a$, and $T$-morphisms
$\phi_a:W_a\to U$ such that

$$
 u\circ\phi_a=r|_{W_a}:W_a\longrightarrow T
 \qquad(a\in J).
$$

Equivalently, $r$ factors through $u$ Zariski locally on $T'$.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $T=\bigcup_kT_k$ using quasi-compactness. For each $k$, base change the surjective etale map $U\to T$ to the affine scheme $T_k$; the resulting family of etale maps is jointly surjective, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement] gives finitely many affine opens in the members of this base-changed family whose images cover $T_k$. Taking the disjoint union over the finitely many $k$ and finitely many opens gives an affine scheme $E$ with a surjective etale map $E\to T$ factoring through $U$. Since $E$ is affine, the map $E\to T$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Since $T$ is quasi-separated, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1) makes this quasi-compact etale map finitely presented.

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), proof paragraph beginning 'Since X is quasi-compact, there exist finitely many affine opens U_i'

proof.text: Prove by induction on $d$ the following claim for every qcqs scheme $X$: for every surjective etale $v:E\to X$ with $E$ quasi-compact and separated, and every geometric fibre of $v$ having at most $d$ points, there are a finite surjective $r:Z\to X$ and a finite open cover of $Z$ on whose members $r$ factors through $E$. The affine-source reduction in step 1 lies in this class: etale is locally quasi-finite [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-quasi-finite], and [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-qc-source-bounded-fibres] gives a uniform finite bound (the number of geometric points is at most the fibre degree). A surjective map with bound $d=0$ has empty target, when the empty finite cover gives the claim. If $d=1$, every geometric fibre has exactly one point, so $v$ is radicial and etale; [lem-weil-pbc-radicial-etale-open] makes it an open immersion, and surjectivity makes it an isomorphism. Take $Z=E\cong X$ and the one-member cover.

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), induction setup and the case d=1

proof.text: For $d>1$, the map $v:E\to X$ in the induction claim is separated and quasi-finite, and is of finite type because etale is locally of finite presentation and its quasi-compact source lies over the qcqs $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1). Apply [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] to obtain a finite (hence integral) $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ and a quasi-compact open immersion $j:E\hookrightarrow\widetilde X$; replace $\widetilde X$ by the scheme-theoretic closure of $E$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]. In $P=E\times_X\widetilde X$, the projection $P\to\widetilde X$ is etale by base change, and the graph $s=(\mathrm{id}_E,j):E\to P$ is a section of $P\to E$. This latter projection is finite by base change of $\pi$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a), hence affine, hence separated. The graph is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]; it is etale as a morphism between schemes etale over $\widetilde X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3), so its image is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] and closed by the closed immersion. Let $W$ be the open-and-closed complement of $s(E)$, so $P=E\amalg W$. The image $V$ of the etale map $W\to\widetilde X$ is open [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] and contains $\widetilde X\setminus E$. The map $W\to V$ is quasi-compact and separated, and $V$ is qcqs. Over the dense open $E$, each geometric fibre of $W$ is the corresponding fibre of $E\to X$ with the diagonal point removed [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-base-change], hence has fewer than $d$ points. The strict bound holds on all of $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-specialization-bound].

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), proof paragraphs applying Lemma 37.43.3 and forming W and V

proof.text: The finite map $\widetilde X\to X$ makes $\widetilde X$ qcqs [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2). The open-and-closed $W\subset E\times_X\widetilde X$ is quasi-compact, since the projection to the quasi-compact $\widetilde X$ is quasi-compact; the map $W\to V$ is separated by base change of the separated $E\to X$ and restriction to an open-and-closed subscheme. Its image $V$ is a quasi-compact open of the quasi-separated $\widetilde X$, hence qcqs. Thus the induction hypothesis applies to the surjective etale $W\to V$ with bound $d-1$, with $W$ quasi-compact and separated and $V$ qcqs, giving a finite surjective $Z\to V$ with finitely many local factorizations through $W$. The composite $Z\to V\hookrightarrow\widetilde X$ is separated, of finite type and everywhere quasi-finite: the first map is finite (hence of finite type) and the second a quasi-compact open immersion; all three properties are preserved by composition. With $\widetilde X$ qcqs, [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] applies to this composite and gives a finite $Z'\to\widetilde X$ with $Z\hookrightarrow Z'$ quasi-compact open. Replace $Z'$ by the scheme-theoretic closure of $Z$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]; then $Z'\times_{\widetilde X}V=Z$. Let $C$ be the reduced closed complement $\widetilde X\setminus V$, so $C\to\widetilde X$ is a closed immersion and hence finite. Both $Z'\to\widetilde X$ and $C\to\widetilde X$ are finite, and their composites with the finite $\widetilde X\to X$ are finite: affine locally, if $A\to B$ and $B\to D$ are module-finite, products of finite module generators for $B/A$ and $D/B$ generate $D/A$. A finite disjoint union of finite maps is finite, so $Z'\amalg C\to X$ is finite; it is surjective since $Z'$ covers $V$ and $C$ covers its complement. On $C\subset E$ it factors through $E$. A point of $Z'\setminus Z$ lies above $\widetilde X\setminus V\subset E$, and a point of $Z$ has a neighbourhood factoring through $W\subset E\times_X\widetilde X$; thus the map locally factors through $E\to X$. This proves the induction claim. Apply it to $E\to T$ from step 1 with the uniform bound $d$ of step 2; the resulting finite surjective $T'\to T$ locally factors through $E$ and hence through the original $U$.

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), induction step after applying the induction hypothesis

proof.text: Call this finite (hence integral) surjection $T'\to T$. Choose a finite affine open cover $T'=\bigcup_jV_j$ refining the opens on which the factorisation through the original $U$ is defined. Write $T'=\varprojlim_iT_i$ with each $T_i\to T$ finite and finitely presented and affine transition maps by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-morphism-limit-of-finite]. By [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] (1), after one common stage each $V_j$ descends to a quasi-compact open $W_{j,i}\subset T_i$; clause (3) of that node identifies $V_j$ with the limit of the $W_{j,k}$ for $k\ge i$, with affine transitions. The $T$-maps $V_j\to U$ therefore descend, after increasing $i$, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-map-limit-factorization], since the etale $U\to T$ is locally of finite presentation. Their equalities over $T$ descend as finite-presentation data by the same limit factorization (or by applying it to the fibre-product equalizer). The opens $W_{j,i}$ cover the stage $T_i$ at a sufficiently large common stage: the finite union $\bigcup_jW_{j,i}$ and $T_i$ itself are quasi-compact opens of $T_i$ with the same preimage $\bigcup_jV_j=T'$ in $T'$, so by [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] (2) their preimages in some later stage $T_{i'}$ agree, that is, $T_{i'}=\bigcup_jW_{j,i'}$. The map $T_i\to T$ is surjective because its composite with $T'\to T_i$ is the surjective $T'\to T$. This stage, its finite open cover, and the descended maps give the stated finite, finitely presented refinement.

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), final paragraph passing from an integral cover to a finite finitely presented stage

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let $U\to T$ be surjective and etale, with $T$ quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. There is a finite, finitely presented, surjective morphism
$r:T'\to T$ and a finite open covering $T'=\bigcup_aW_a$ such that every
$W_a\to T$ factors through $U\to T$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Choose finitely many affine opens $U_a\subset U$ whose images cover $T$ and
replace $U$ by their disjoint union. The resulting map is quasi-compact,
separated, etale, and has a finite upper bound $d$ on the cardinalities of
its geometric fibres. We induct on $d$. If $d=1$, the map is radicial and
etale, hence an open immersion; surjectivity makes it an isomorphism.

For $d>1$, apply the affine form of Zariski's Main Theorem to the separated
quasi-finite map $U\to T$: adjoining to $\mathcal O_T$ the integral elements
of the quasi-coherent algebra $u_*\mathcal O_U$ gives an integral
$\pi:\widetilde T\to T$ and a quasi-compact open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow\widetilde T$. Replace $\widetilde T$ by the
scheme-theoretic closure of $U$, so $U$ is schematically dense. The diagonal
section gives an open-and-closed decomposition

$$
U\times_T\widetilde T=U\amalg W.
$$

The image $V$ of $W\to\widetilde T$ is open and contains
$\widetilde T\setminus U$. Over a point of the dense open $U$, the fibre of
$W\to V$ is the fibre of $U\to T$ with the diagonal point removed, so it has
fewer than $d$ points. The number of points in a separated etale fibre
cannot increase under specialization: after writing the map locally as a
finite disjoint union of Jacobian etale algebra presentations, distinct idempotents at a
specialization lift to distinct idempotents at a generization. Thus every
geometric fibre of $W\to V$ has cardinality $<d$.

By induction there is an integral surjection $Z\to V$, locally factoring
through $W$. Apply the same integral-closure construction to
$Z\to\widetilde T$ and take the closure $Z'$ of $Z$; then
$Z'\times_{\widetilde T}V=Z$. If $C$ is the reduced closed complement
$\widetilde T\setminus V$, then $C\subset U$, and
$Z'\amalg C\to T$ is integral and surjective. Near a point of $Z$ it
factors through $W\to U$; near a point of $Z'\setminus Z$ it factors through
$C\subset U$. Hence it locally factors through the original cover.

Finally write this integral morphism as the inverse limit of its finite
finitely presented $T$-subalgebras. Choose finitely many affine opens on
which the factorization through $U$ is defined. Each open, each map to $U$,
the equalities over $T$, and surjectivity descend to a common finite stage:
the first three assertions are finite-presentation data, while failure of
surjectivity has quasi-compact open image and would persist after pullback to
the limit. That common stage is the required $T'$. This is the construction
located at Tag `09Z0`, with the degree induction and final finite stage
made explicit.

tool_uses.why: The induction needs quasi-finiteness of the etale map.
The induction needs a uniform bound on geometric fibre cardinalities.
The induction embeds quasi-finite separated covers as opens in finite covers.
The diagonal argument counts geometric points after base change.
The final step expresses the integral cover as finite finitely presented stages.
The final step descends each quasi-compact open and identifies its limit.
